See also: [Bowling form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_form "Bowling form") and [Bowling ball §Effect of delivery characteristics on ball motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_ball#Effect_of_delivery_characteristics_on_ball_motion "Bowling ball")

Three widely recognized categories are _stroker, cranker_ and _tweener_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2011-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2004-25)

*   Strokers—using the most "classic" bowling form—tend to keep the shoulders square to the foul line and develop only a moderately high backswing, achieving modest ball rotation ("rev") rates and ball speeds, which thus limit hook potential and kinetic energy delivered to the pins.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2011-24) Strokers rely on accuracy and repeatability, and benefit from the high entry angles that reactive resin balls enable.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2011-24)
*   Crankers tend to open (rotate) the shoulders and use strong wrist and arm action in concert with a high backswing, achieving higher rev rates and ball speeds, thus maximizing hook potential and kinetic energy.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2011-24) Crankers rely on speed and power, but may leave splits rarely left by strokers.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2011-24)
*   Tweeners (derived from "in-between") have styles that fall between those of strokers and crankers; the term is considered by some to include _power strokers_ who combine the high rev rates of crankers with the smooth delivery of strokers.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2011-24)

#### Alternative deliveries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Alternative deliveries")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/20240621_John_Furey_bowling_ball_release.jpg/120px-20240621_John_Furey_bowling_ball_release.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20240621_John_Furey_bowling_ball_release.jpg)

PBA bowler John Furey uses a **conventional (one-handed) delivery.** Finger rotation can induce [axis rotation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_bowling#Axis_rotation "Glossary of bowling"), causing the ball to hook (curve).

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/20190818_Zach_Wilkins_two-handed_bowling_-_screenshot_before_release.png/330px-20190818_Zach_Wilkins_two-handed_bowling_-_screenshot_before_release.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20190818_Zach_Wilkins_two-handed_bowling_-_screenshot_before_release.png)

**Two-handed delivery:** Both hands retain contact with the ball until just before the release.  
Though it is often incorrectly called a two-handed _release_, the actual release involves a single dominant hand for most bowlers.  
For most two-handed deliveries, the thumb is never inserted into the ball in the first place, allowing a high [rev rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_bowling#Rev_rate "Glossary of bowling") and resultant hook.  
(shown: Zach Wilkins)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/ClaraJulianaGuerrero.jpg/250px-ClaraJulianaGuerrero.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ClaraJulianaGuerrero.jpg)

**Delivery styles** often involve a long follow-through and widely extended balance arm and leg. (shown: [Clara Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clara_Guerrero "Clara Guerrero"))

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e2/20190818_Zach_Wilkins_two-handed_bowling.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

**Video: The two-handed delivery**, widely popularized by [Jason Belmonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Belmonte "Jason Belmonte"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WSJ20090205-26) increases potential [rev rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_bowling#Rev_rate "Glossary of bowling") and hook.   
(shown: Zach Wilkins)

*   So-called _[two-handed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-handed\_bowling "Two-handed bowling")_ bowling, first popularized late in the 2000s by Australian [Jason Belmonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Belmonte "Jason Belmonte"), involves not inserting the thumb into any thumbhole, with the opposite hand supporting and guiding the ball throughout _almost_ the entire forward swing.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WSJ20090205-26) This delivery style, involving more athletic ability, is increasingly popular with younger bowlers and technically still involves a one-handed _release._[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBcom_20161216-27) It allows the inserted fingers to generate higher revolution rates and thus attain greater hook potential than with a thumb-in-hole approach.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFreemanHatfield2018Chapter_5_(%22You_Say_You_Want_a_Revolution%22)-28) In contrast, in what is literally a two-handed delivery and release, children or physically challenged players use both hands to deliver the ball forward from between the legs or from the chest.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-KegelGlossary20100320-29)
*   _No-thumb_ bowling involves only a single hand during the forward swing, without the thumb inserted. The ball is often balanced on the wrist and forearm of the delivery hand for this technique.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBcom2hand2011-30) A successful professional who uses the one-handed no-thumb delivery is [Tom Daugherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Daugherty "Tom Daugherty").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TD-onehand-31)

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Bowling-UFO-release.jpg/250px-Bowling-UFO-release.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bowling-UFO-release.jpg)

The "UFO" or "helicopter" release: the thumb faces the body, while the middle and ring fingers face the pins.

*   The _spinner_ style, which is mainly popular in parts of Asia, has a "helicopter" or "UFO" release that involves rotating the wrist to impart a high (vertical) axis of rotation that causes the bowling ball to spin like a [top](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinning_top "Spinning top") while traveling straight down the lane.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2004-25) Usually involving a lighter (10–12 pound) ball, the spinner style takes advantage of the ball deflection from the head pin to then "walk down" the other visible pins and cause [domino effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domino_effect "Domino effect") diagonally through the pins.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Styles2004-25)
*   In the _backup_ (or _reverse hook_) release, the wrist rotates clockwise (for right hand releases) or counter-clockwise (for left hand releases), causing the ball to hook in a direction opposite to that of conventional releases.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBcomBackup20180909-32)

### Grips

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Grips")]

A _conventional grip_, used on non-customized house balls and some custom-drilled balls, involves insertion of fingers to the second knuckle.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-GFtrib20171203-33) A _fingertip grip_, involving insertion of fingers only to the first knuckle, enables greater revolution rates and resultant hook potential.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-GFtrib20171203-33) A _thumbless grip_, often used by so-called "two-handed" bowlers, maximizes ball rotational speed ("rev rate").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-GFtrib20171203-33)

## Pins and scoring

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Pins and scoring")]

### String pinsetters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: String pinsetters")]

In 2023, the [USBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bowling_Congress "United States Bowling Congress") certified [string pinsetters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_bowling "String bowling") (SPs) without any score adjustment compared to mechanical freefall pinsetters (FFPs), while acknowledging that bowlers have slightly lower averages when using SPs.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCreport_2023-34) String pinsetters are less expensive and easier to maintain, motivating bowling centers to phase them in.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Newser_20230122-35)

### Traditional scoring

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Traditional scoring")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Bowlstrike.PNG/250px-Bowlstrike.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bowlstrike.PNG)

Traditional scoring of a [strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_(bowling) "Strike (bowling)"): 
Frame one: 10 + (3 + 6) = 19

 Frame two: 3 + 6 = 9 → Total = 28

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Bowlspare.png/250px-Bowlspare.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bowlspare.png)

Traditional scoring of a [spare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spare_(bowling) "Spare (bowling)"): 
Frame one: (7 + 3) + 4 = 14

 Frame two: 4 + 2 = 6 → Total = 20

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/20191106_Bowling_-_scratch_and_handicap_scoring.png/250px-20191106_Bowling_-_scratch_and_handicap_scoring.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20191106_Bowling_-_scratch_and_handicap_scoring.png)

Though the second bowler's scratch score 183 is higher than the first bowler's scratch score 181, the first bowler's higher handicap (58 vs. 53) causes his total 239 to exceed the second bowler's total 236.

In traditional scoring,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCch2-Rules2018-2019-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBcom_20121208-37) one point is scored for each pin that is knocked over, and when fewer than all ten pins are knocked down in two rolls in a frame (an _open frame_), the frame is scored with the total number of pins knocked down. However, when all ten pins are knocked down with either the first or second rolls of a frame (a _mark_), _bonus_ pins are awarded as follows:

*   **[Strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_(bowling) "Strike (bowling)")**: When all ten pins are knocked down on the first roll (marked "X" on the scorescreen), the frame receives ten pins _plus_ a bonus of pinfall on the next two _rolls_ (not necessarily the next two _frames_). A strike in the tenth (final) frame receives two extra rolls for bonus pins.
*   **[Spare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spare_(bowling) "Spare (bowling)")**: When a second roll of a frame is needed to knock down all ten pins (marked "/" on the scorescreen), the frame receives ten pins _plus_ a bonus of pinfall in the next _roll_ (not necessarily the next _frame_). A spare in the first two rolls in the tenth (final) frame receives a third roll for bonus pins.
*   [**Split**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_(bowling) "Split (bowling)"): When pins that have not yet been knocked down form a gap that is at least one pin apart, therefore making it very difficult to get a spare (marked by highlighting the number of the roll in red on the scorescreen).
*   **Gutter**: When no pins are hit on a roll (marked "-" on the scorescreen).

The maximum score is 300, achieved by getting twelve strikes in a row within the same game (known as a [perfect game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_game_(bowling) "Perfect game (bowling)")).

### World Bowling scoring

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: World Bowling scoring")]

The [World Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bowling "World Bowling") scoring system—described as "current frame scoring"[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-InsideTheGames20160220-38)—awards pins as follows:

*   A strike is 30 pins, regardless of ensuing rolls' results.
*   A spare is 10 pins, plus the pinfall on first roll of the _current_ frame.
*   An open frame is the total pinfall of the current frame.

The maximum score is 300, achieved with ten consecutive strikes (as opposed to twelve in traditional scoring), but with no bonus pins received in the tenth frame.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WeberCup20160729-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-InsideTheGames20160221-40)

World Bowling scoring is thought to make bowling easier to follow than with traditional scoring,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WeberCup20160729-39) increase television viewership,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-InsideTheGames20160220-38) and help bowling to become an [Olympic sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sports "Olympic sports").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-InsideTheGames20160220-38)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-InsideTheGames20160221-40)

#### Variant of World Bowling scoring

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Variant of World Bowling scoring")]

Another variant of scoring, a 12-frame system introduced at the November 2014 [World Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bowling "World Bowling") Tour (WBT) finals, resembles golf's [match play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Match_play "Match play") scoring in counting the greater number of _frames_ won rather than measuring accumulated pinfall score.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WB201410-41) A frame may be won immediately by a higher pincount on the first roll of the frame, and a match may be won when one player is ahead by more frames than remain of the possible 12 frames.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WB201410-41) This variant reduces match length and scoring complexity for two-player matches.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WB201410-41)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: History")]

For a more comprehensive history of other forms of bowling that pre-date tenpin bowling, see Bowling §History.

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Early history")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/18200610_Ball_and_Ten_Pin_Alley_-_Indiana_Centinel_%28Vincennes%29.png/250px-18200610_Ball_and_Ten_Pin_Alley_-_Indiana_Centinel_%28Vincennes%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:18200610_Ball_and_Ten_Pin_Alley_-_Indiana_Centinel_(Vincennes).png)

An early (1820) newspaper ad features a "Ball and Ten Pin Alley" to attract customers to a "Baking and Confectionary Business".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-IndianaCentinel_18200610-2)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/18290622_Promoting_Observance_of_the_Sabbath_-_image_of_bowling_alleys_-_Georgia_Journal.png/330px-18290622_Promoting_Observance_of_the_Sabbath_-_image_of_bowling_alleys_-_Georgia_Journal.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:18290622_Promoting_Observance_of_the_Sabbath_-_image_of_bowling_alleys_-_Georgia_Journal.png)

An 1829 newspaper editorial describes those who frequent bowling alleys and taverns: "the young, the frivolous, the headstrong, ... men of coarser passions and appetites, and fond of more riotous pleasures"[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-GaJournal_18290622-42)—reflecting the often negative image bowling had.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/18380310_Evasions_of_Law_-_Logansport_Telegraph.png/250px-18380310_Evasions_of_Law_-_Logansport_Telegraph.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:18380310_Evasions_of_Law_-_Logansport_Telegraph.png)

An 1838 Indiana newspaper describes how tenpin bowling was devised to evade a [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore") statute prohibiting nine-pin bowling.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Logansport_18380310-44)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/18390629_Nine_or_ten_pin_bowling_alley_-_Logansport_Telegraph.png/250px-18390629_Nine_or_ten_pin_bowling_alley_-_Logansport_Telegraph.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:18390629_Nine_or_ten_pin_bowling_alley_-_Logansport_Telegraph.png)

An 1839 liquor license ordinance prohibited gambling in "any ball, nine or ten pin alley"—associating bowling with gambling and games having a "demoralizing tendency".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-LogansportTelegraph_18390629-45)

Modern tenpin bowling derives mainly from the German [Kegelspiel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine-pin_bowling "Nine-pin bowling"), or kegeling, which used nine pins set in a diamond formation.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) The enjoyment of kegeling by German peasants contrasted with (lawn) [bowls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowls "Bowls") that was reserved for the upper classes, consistent with tenpin bowling's enduring reputation as a common man's sport.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)

A [_circa_ 1810 painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1810_Ransome_&_Son_-_painting_-_outdoor_ten_pin_bowling.jpg "File:1810 Ransome & Son - painting - outdoor ten pin bowling.jpg") of [Ipswich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich "Ipswich"), England, shows a man bowling outdoors with a triangular formation of ten pins.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Pluckhahn_19881200-1) An outdoor version of tenpin bowling was [advertised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:18280426_Auction_of_Chequers_Public_House_with_Bowling_Green,_Ten-pin_and_Skittle_grounds_-_Ipswich_Journal.jpg "File:18280426 Auction of Chequers Public House with Bowling Green, Ten-pin and Skittle grounds - Ipswich Journal.jpg"), also in Ipswich, at least as early as 1828.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-IpswichJournal_18280426-46)

An 1841 Connecticut law banned ninepin bowling because of its perceived association with gambling and crime, and people were said to circumvent the prohibition by adding a tenth pin.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NshoreNews20180330-47) Other locations (e.g., 1838, re [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore")[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Logansport_18380310-44) and 1842, [Charles Dickens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dickens "Charles Dickens") re New York[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NYDailyNews_20120207-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NYHerald_18421108-49)) also recount that strategy. Even earlier, an 1834 Washington, D.C. ordinance had limited the time (before 8 p.m. and not on Sundays) and place (more than 100 yards from inhabited houses) of "nine pin and ten pins" or "any game in the likeness or imitation thereof ... played with any number of pins whatsoever".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NationalIntelligencer_18340807-50) U.S. newspapers referred to "ten pin alleys" at least as early as 1820[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-IndianaCentinel_18200610-2) (also later in the 1820s[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-MdRepublican_18210526-51) and in the 1830s[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WashDailyNatnlIntelligencer_18300402-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DailyNationalIntelligencer_18310621-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WashGlobe_18320628-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BostonMorningPost_18330518-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DailySavannahRepublican_18340503-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Nationalintelligencer_18360924-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-GlobeWashDC_18370318-58)).

In the mid-1800s, various alternatives to free-standing pins received U.S. patents to solve perceived problems in pinsetting and ball return, aiming to avoid the need for human pinsetters to perform these functions. One scheme (1851) involved pins with spherical bases that when hit by a ball merely fell over, in place, to be rotated back to a vertical position.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-59) A second arrangement (1853) involved resetting the pins via cords descending from respective pin bottoms to weights beneath the pin deck.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-60) Another design (1869) involved suspending the pins with overhead cords.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Patent-61)

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/18940502_Bowling_alley_number_191_by_H._Schile.jpg/250px-18940502_Bowling_alley_number_191_by_H._Schile.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:18940502_Bowling_alley_number_191_by_H._Schile.jpg)

This 1894 depiction emphasizes the social nature of the sport. Balls of different sizes are used for games other than tenpin.

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/1895_Bowling_lockers.jpg/250px-1895_Bowling_lockers.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1895_Bowling_lockers.jpg)

An 1895 advertisement for bowling lockers (price: $6.00 each section) suggests the attire and facilities used by bowlers of the era.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BowlingLockers_1895-62)

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Bowling_alley_at_the_Pleasant_Beach_Hotel%2C_Bainbridge_Island%2C_ca_1898_%28HESTER_61%29.jpeg/250px-Bowling_alley_at_the_Pleasant_Beach_Hotel%2C_Bainbridge_Island%2C_ca_1898_%28HESTER_61%29.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bowling_alley_at_the_Pleasant_Beach_Hotel,_Bainbridge_Island,_ca_1898_(HESTER_61).jpeg)

Bowling alley at the Pleasant Beach Hotel, Bainbridge Island, Washington (c. 1898)

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/Bowling_alley_1908.jpg/250px-Bowling_alley_1908.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bowling_alley_1908.jpg)

Human pinsetters (Pittsburgh, c. 1908) preceded automated mechanical pinsetters.

In 1884, the [Brunswick Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunswick_Corporation "Brunswick Corporation") became the first American bowling ball manufacturer, and by 1905[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-OregonJournal_19051107-63) introduced the Mineralite (hard rubber) ball that was considered so revolutionary over wooden balls that it was displayed at the [Century of Progress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_of_Progress "Century of Progress") Exposition in 1934.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) In 1886, [Joe Thum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Thum "Joe Thum")—who would become known as the "father of bowling"—began opening bowling alleys including at [401 Greenwich Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/401_Greenwich_Street "401 Greenwich Street") in the [Tribeca West Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_West_Historic_District "Tribeca West Historic District")[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NYTimes_19350110-64) and over decades strove to elevate the sport's image to compete with upper-class diversions such as theaters and opera houses.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)

In 1875, delegates from [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") and [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn") bowling clubs formed the National Bowling Association (NBA) to standardize rules, but disagreements prevailed.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBChistoryOfBowling-65) In 1887 [Albert G. Spalding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Spalding "Albert Spalding") wrote _Standard Rules for Bowling in the United States_, and in the mid-1890s the United Bowling Clubs (UBC) was organized with 120 members.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) The [American Bowling Congress (ABC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bowling_Congress "United States Bowling Congress") was established in 1895, followed by the [Women's International Bowling Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_International_Bowling_Congress "Women's International Bowling Congress") (WIBC) in the 1910s, such organizations promoting standardized rules and striving to improve the sport's image.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)

From 1920 to 1929, the number of ABC-sanctioned alleys grew from 450 to about 2,000, with [Prohibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States "Prohibition in the United States") leading to the growth of family-appropriate "dry" alleys.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) The 1933 repeal of Prohibition allowed breweries to sponsor teams and bowlers, adding to bowling's reputation as a working-class sport.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) Though at the turn of the twentieth century most bowling alleys were small establishments, post-Prohibition bowling lanes shifted from side entertainment at fancy Victorian venues or seedier saloons to independent establishments that embraced the [Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") style and fit the era's perceived "need for speed".[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)

### 1940s to early 1960s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: 1940s to early 1960s")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/2%2C208%2C605_Bowling_pin_setting_apparatus_-_patent.png/250px-2%2C208%2C605_Bowling_pin_setting_apparatus_-_patent.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2,208,605_Bowling_pin_setting_apparatus_-_patent.png)

Actual text from one of Gottfried Schmidt's patents, this one from an application filed in 1936 and describing how his "bowling pin setting apparatus" can pick up and replace pins even if they were off their proper spots[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Patent2208605-66)

Gottfried Schmidt invented the first mechanical [pinsetter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinsetter "Pinsetter") in his garage in 1936, one implementation of which was publicly exhibited in 1946 before AMF placed a production model into service in 1952.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TenPinBowlingHistory2004-67)

Bowling in the U.S. flourished during World War II, when employers sponsored teams in industrial leagues to boost worker morale.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-CWRU_2017-68) The U.S. government's "Bowling for Health" campaigns promoted bowling for its health benefits, and the military made bowling centers a regular feature on military bases.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitMetroTimes_20140527-69)

Initially, [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bowling_Congress "United States Bowling Congress") and [WIBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_International_Bowling_Congress "Women's International Bowling Congress") constitutions had banned non-[Caucasians](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Caucasian "wikt:Caucasian") from membership.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-CWRU_2017-68)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TNBA_organization-70) ABC bylaws had included a "[white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans")-males-only" clause since its inception in the 1890s, but numerous lobbying efforts and legal actions after World War II by civil rights and labor organizations led to a reversal of this policy in 1950.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Integration-71) The National Negro Bowling Association, formed in 1939 and renamed The National Bowling Association (TNBA) five years later, had served minority bowlers before ABC and WIBC membership restrictions were removed in 1950.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TNBA_organization-70) TNBA remains today, open to men and women without regard to race, creed or color.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TNBA_organization-70)

The 1940s through the 1970s became known as the "golden age of bowling",[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72) with ABC membership growing from 700,000 (1940), to 1.1 million (1947), to 2.3 million (1958), to 4.5 million (1963),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) Women's International Bowling Congress membership growing from 82,000 (1940) to 866,000 (1958),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) American Junior Bowling Congress membership growing from 8,000 (1940) to 175,000 (1958),[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) and sanctioned individual lanes growing from 44,500 (1947) to 159,000 (1963).[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43)

Bowling's growth was fueled by the deployment of automatic mechanical pinsetters by AMF (1952) and Brunswick (1955), television broadcasts (said to be "ubiquitous" in the 1950s), modernization and stylization of establishments with amenities to attract broader clientele, and formation of [bowling leagues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_league "Bowling league").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) Though President Truman had installed a bowling alley in the White House in 1947,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) a report of the American Society of Planning Officials in 1958 characterized bowling alleys as the "poor man's country club".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73)

[Sports agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent")[Eddie Elias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Elias "Eddie Elias") founded the [Professional Bowlers Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Bowlers_Association "Professional Bowlers Association") (PBA) in 1958 with 33 members, and the first PBA tournaments began in 1959.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TenPinBowlingHistory2004-67) The _[Pro Bowlers Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional\_Bowlers\_Tour "Professional Bowlers Tour")_ TV program aired from 1962[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1960s-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBAhistory-75) through 1997.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1990s-76)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBAhistory-75)

In the 1930s and 1940s, professional bowling was dominated by "beer leagues" with many of the best bowlers sponsored by beer companies, but by 1965 the PBA tour was televised nationally on ABC Sports with sponsors such as [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Coca-Cola_Company "The Coca-Cola Company") and [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72)

In parallel with professional bowling was "action bowling" or "pot bowling"—bowling matches based on monetary bets—historically associated with the New York underworld from the 1940s to the 1970s.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72)

### Late 1960s to 1980

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Late 1960s to 1980")]

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/The_Ronettes_and_Murray_the_K.jpg/250px-The_Ronettes_and_Murray_the_K.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Ronettes_and_Murray_the_K.jpg)

[The Ronettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ronettes "The Ronettes") and New York disc jockey [Murray the K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_the_K "Murray the K") using bowling as a promotional device in 1962, during the "golden age of bowling"[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72)

The first ten-pin lanes in Europe had been installed in Sweden in 1909, but attempts to popularize the sport in Europe were unsuccessful over the next several decades, though hundreds of lanes were installed on U.S. military bases in the U.K. during World War II.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BritannicaBowling-77) Various countries developed the sport to some extent, and the Fédération Internationale des Quilleurs (FIQ; now [World Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bowling "World Bowling")) was formed in 1952 to coordinate international amateur competition.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BritannicaBowling-77)

A firmer establishment of the sport began in the U.K. in 1960 in London ([Stamford Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Hill "Stamford Hill")) in January 1960,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TenPin2014-78) and the [British Tenpin Bowling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Tenpin_Bowling_Association "British Tenpin Bowling Association") (BTBA) was formed the following year.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BritannicaBowling-77) The first British made tenpin was by H Massil and sons who received the permit no.1 from the BTBA.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-79) Various other countries, including Australia, Mexico and Japan, adopted the trend over the ensuing decade.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BritannicaBowling-77) After initial [faddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fad "Fad") growth in the U.K., however, the sport did not thrive as it did in the U.S., and by the 1970s many British bowling alleys were converted to serve competing pastimes, such as bingo.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Leicestershire20170801-80)

The "Lane Master" automatic lane cleaning and conditioning machine was first deployed in the 1960s.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1960s-74)

In the 1960s and early 1970s, top bowling professionals made twice as much money as [NFL football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") stars, received million-dollar endorsement contracts, and were treated as international celebrities.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72) The $100,000 Firestone Tournament of Champions launched in 1965, in a decade that saw ABC membership peak at almost 4.6 million male bowlers.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1960s-74) The number of sanctioned bowling alleys peaked at about 12,000 in the mid-1960s,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) mostly in blue-collar urban areas,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Buzzle20170722-81) and Women's International Bowling Congress (WIBC) membership peaked at 4.2 million members in 1979.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1970s-82)

In the late 1960s, the participation sport of bowling found itself competing with spectator sports and outdoor recreational activities.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-StJames2002-43) The number of certified bowling centers was to eventually decline from its 1960s high of 12,000[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) to 6,542 in 1998[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Buzzle20170722-81) and 3,976 in 2013.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) The decline was noted acutely in waning league participation over the intervening decades.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BowlingAlone-83)

### 1980 to 2000

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: 1980 to 2000")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-Z0318-030%2C_Berlin%2C_Sport-_und_Erholungszentrum%2C_Bowlingbahn.jpg/250px-Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-Z0318-030%2C_Berlin%2C_Sport-_und_Erholungszentrum%2C_Bowlingbahn.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bundesarchiv_Bild_183-Z0318-030,_Berlin,_Sport-_und_Erholungszentrum,_Bowlingbahn.jpg)

A bowling alley in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") (1981) with early electronic displays

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/1900-_Membership_in_bowling_leagues.svg/250px-1900-_Membership_in_bowling_leagues.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1900-_Membership_in_bowling_leagues.svg)

League participation peaked in the 1960s and 1970s.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-CNN_20250824-84) League bowling was used as a barometer of social engagement in political scientist [Robert D. Putnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_D._Putnam "Robert D. Putnam")'s book, _[Bowling Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling\_Alone "Bowling Alone")_ (2000).

Tournament prize funds in the 1980s included the PBA National Championship ($135,000, its largest) and the Firestone Tournament of Champions ($150,000), and PBA membership approached 2,500.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1980s-85) Ten-pin bowling became an exhibition sport at the [1988 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") (Seoul),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBcom_SportOrGame-3)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1980s-85) has been [a medal sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_at_the_Pan_American_Games "Bowling at the Pan American Games") since its debut at the [1991 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Pan_American_Games "1991 Pan American Games") (Havana),[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1990s-76) and was included in the [1998 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Commonwealth_Games "1998 Commonwealth Games") (Kuala Lumpur).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-CommonwealthGames1998-86)

Outside elite and professional bowling, participation in leagues—traditionally the more profitable end of the business—declined from a 1980 peak (8 million), compelling alleys to further diversify into entertainment amenities.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) As busier, two-earner households became more common in the 1980s to make league participation more difficult, the number of spectator sports and competing leisure time opportunities (jogging, tennis, skiing) grew.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DeptEducation_2011-87) While league bowling decreased by 40 percent between 1980 and 1993, the total number of bowlers actually increased by 10 percent during that period, with nearly 80 million Americans going bowling at least once during 1993.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BowlingAlone-83) In 1995, the National Bowling Stadium (Reno, Nevada) was constructed at a cost of $47.5 million, but the PBA Pro Bowlers Tour TV program was canceled in 1997 after a 35-year run.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WashPost19970621-88)

In 1991, equipment manufacturer DBA Products released "The Lane Walker"—the first computer-driven lane cleaning and oiling machine, programmable to clean up to 50 lanes.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1990s-76)

The early 1990s brought the development of reactive resin ("reactive") balls with chemically "tacky" surfaces that enhance traction to dramatically enhance hook and substantially increase the likelihood of striking, raising average scores even for less experienced bowlers.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBevolution2012-11)

In 1998, the Sporting Goods Manufacturers Association (SGMA) president attributed an increase in popularity to bowling alley remodeling, technological innovations in balls and lanes, computerized scoring, and promotion by bowling organizations.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Throw-89)

### 2000 to present

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: 2000 to present")]

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/North_Korea_Bowling_Alley.jpg/250px-North_Korea_Bowling_Alley.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_Korea_Bowling_Alley.jpg)

Example of a modern bowling alley in [Pyongyang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyongyang "Pyongyang") (2010)

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/20241112_US_Patent_12%2C138%2C527_-_String_pinsetter_operation.gif/250px-20241112_US_Patent_12%2C138%2C527_-_String_pinsetter_operation.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20241112_US_Patent_12,138,527_-_String_pinsetter_operation.gif)

In 2023, the USBC began certifying [string pinsetters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_bowling "String bowling"),[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-QubicaAMF_drawings-90) which are being installed in a growing number of bowling centers because of their reduced cost and maintenance requirements.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCscoringReport_202511-91)

External video
[![Image 34: video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg) YouTube short: [String pinsetter operation](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/9AdpAlxjv2s)

From 1998 to 2013, the number of American bowling centers fell by one quarter.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73) Similarly, in the two decades following 1997, the number of USBC-certified _lanes_—also indicative of business viability—declined by one-third.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCdata1997--92) This business decline is often attributed to waning league participation: USBC membership—indicative of league participation that was the main source of revenue—declined by two-thirds in those two decades,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCdata1997--92) and the portion of alley revenue attributable to leagues is estimated to have dropped from 70% to 40%.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WhiteHutchinson2007-93) Political scientist [Robert D. Putnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_D._Putnam "Robert D. Putnam")'s book _[Bowling Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling\_Alone "Bowling Alone")_ (2000) asserts, with some controversy, that the retreat from league bowling epitomizes a broader societal decline in social, civic and community engagement in the U.S.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DetroitFP20150509-73)

As an indication of the decline, [AMF Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Machine_and_Foundry "American Machine and Foundry"), the largest operator of bowling centers in the world at the time, filed for [Chapter 11 bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapter_11_bankruptcy "Chapter 11 bankruptcy") in 2001, and again in 2012.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Reuters_20121113-94) By 2013, AMF Bowling had merged with New York–based Bowlmor (no relation to the defunct, 1940s-founded _Bowl-Mor_ firm that invented the [automatic pinsetter for candlepin bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinsetter#Candlepin_pinsetters "Pinsetter")), the company becoming known as [Bowlmor AMF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowlmor_AMF "Bowlmor AMF").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Pehub_20130701-95)

In 2000, three former tech industry executives bought a debt-laden PBA—which saw its 36-year television contract with ABC Sports end in 1997—and turned it from a [non-profit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization") league into a for-profit organization, and invested heavily in marketing.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-CNN20000322-96) The January 2005 merger of four U.S. bowling organizations to form the USBC formed a "central [brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand "Brand")" aiming to grow the sport.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCabout-97) Beginning late in the decade of the 2000s, the [two-handed approach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowling_form#Two-handed_approach "Bowling form") became popularized, first by Australian [Jason Belmonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Belmonte "Jason Belmonte"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WSJ20090205-26) with some hoping that the controversial delivery style would boost popularity of the sport.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WSJ20090205-26) In January 2013, the eight-team PBA League began competition,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBAleague201301-98) the strategy being that basing teams in specific geographic localities would generate viewer enthusiasm and corporate sponsorship in the same manner as teams in other professional sports.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Bleacher20130123-99) Still, continuing the reversal of bowling's peak popularity in the 1960s, in the 2012–2013 season the average yearly winnings of the ten highest-earning PBA competitors was less than US$155,000, and the average for the remaining 250 competitors was $6,500—all much less than a rookie [NFL football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") player's minimum base salary of $375,000.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72)

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Cosmicbowling2.jpg/250px-Cosmicbowling2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cosmicbowling2.jpg)

To attract a broader range of patrons, many bowling centers offer "cosmic bowling" (shown) and host other special events.

Estimates of the number of total (league and non-league) bowlers in the U.S. have varied, from 82 million (1997, International Bowling Museum)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WashPost19970621-88) to 51.6 million (2007, research firm White Hutchinson)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WhiteHutchinson2007-93) to 71 million (2009, USBC),[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCpressroom2010-100) the USBC stating in 2019 that bowling is still the #1 participation sport in the U.S.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCpressRoom20190129-101) More broadly, the [International Bowling Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Bowling_Museum "International Bowling Museum") stated in 2016 that bowling is played by 95 million people in more than 90 countries.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BowlingMuseumHistory2016-102) In an era of continual decline in league participation,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCdata1997--92)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WashPost19970621-88) bowling centers promoted "party bowling"[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Priceonomics20140321-72) and black-light-and-disco-ball "cosmic bowling"[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WashPost19970621-88) and experienced a shift from blue-collar participants to open-play (non-league) family-oriented clientele in combined bowling and entertainment centers.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WhiteHutchinson2007-93)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DenverPost_20240315-103) Some offered laser tag, indoor playgrounds, go-karting, climbing walls, arcade games, skating rinks, gourmet restaurants, and nightclub-style bowling lounges.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DeptEducation_2011-87) School sport programs expanded, the USBC stating that more than 5,000 high schools offered bowling as a competitive sport, with 50,000 student bowlers participating in 2009–2010.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DeptEducation_2011-87) In 2011, the Bowling Proprietor's Association of America stated that more than 60% of U.S. bowlers were under age 34, that 46% were girls and women, and that children participated in bowling at a higher rate than any other population group.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DeptEducation_2011-87)

Since 1997, Bowlero Corporation (later called [Lucky Strike Entertainment Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Strike_Entertainment_Corporation "Lucky Strike Entertainment Corporation")) acquired competitors [AMF Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AMF_Bowling "AMF Bowling"), [Brunswick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunswick_Bowling_&_Billiards "Brunswick Bowling & Billiards") and [Lucky Strike Lanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Strike_Lanes "Lucky Strike Lanes"), and purchased the [Professional Bowlers Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Bowlers_Association "Professional Bowlers Association") (PBA).[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DenverPost_20240315-103) In the early 2020s, U.S. bowlers experienced a surge in fees attributed by experts to consolidation of big chains, facilities upgrades, and effects of the COVID-19 pandemic when bowling alleys were deemed "non-essential businesses".[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-DenverPost_20240315-103)

In contrast to the U.S., the 2000s and 2010s brought a bowling renaissance in the U.K., achieved by accommodating sophisticated modern tastes by providing (for example) [retro-style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro_style "Retro style") bowling alleys outfitted with 1950s [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana_(culture) "Americana (culture)"), "boutique bowling", "VIP lanes", and cameras for instant replays, and by rejuvenating bowling "alleys" into diverse-entertainment bowling "centres".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Guardian20060319-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Guardian20170722-105) The population of ten-pin bowling centres grew from a low of barely 50 (in the 1980s) to over 200 (2006),[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Guardian20060319-104) with almost a third of Britons going bowling in 2016 and league participation growing over 20% over two years (2015–2017).[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-Guardian20170722-105)

Though ten-pin bowling was a demonstration sport in the [1988 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") (Seoul)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-PBSthe1980s-85) and has been included in the [Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan_American_Games "Pan American Games") since 1991,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-GlobalNews20150401-106) after making the shortlist for inclusion in the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") (Tokyo), it was cut.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TimesUnion20181207-107) One commentator noted that the sport's limited geographic popularity (the U.S., Australia and a few European and South American countries), and aging demographic of those who follow the sport, make it difficult to convince an Olympic Committee that wants to appeal to youth.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TimesUnion20181207-107)

## Bowling organizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Bowling organizations")]

> In bowling, we are trying to deliver a heavy 14 or 15 pound bowling ball over the foul line at about an average speed of 16 or 17 miles per hour, apply a rotational force to the ball in order to gain an effective hook motion, hit a one inch sighting target on the lane, and accurately impact the pocket 60 feet away while smashing down about 36 pounds of lumber. There are certainly easier things to do.

—Rich Carrubba, 2013[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BBcom_-108)

### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: International")]

[World Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bowling "World Bowling") (WB) was formed in 2014 from component organizations of the _Fédération Internationale des Quilleurs_ (FIQ, International Federation of Bowlers), which in 1952 developed from the International Bowling Association (IBA) which began operations in 1926.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WBabout2019-109) Since 1979 the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") has recognized the FIQ, and later, WB, as the sport's world governing body.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WBabout2019-109) WB establishes rules for the uniform practice of bowling throughout the world, and promotes bowling as an Olympic sport.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WBabout2019-109) The [World Tenpin Bowling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Tenpin_Bowling_Association "World Tenpin Bowling Association") "membership discipline" (component organization) of WB serves the amateur sport of ten-pin bowling worldwide, adopting uniform playing rules and equipment specifications.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-WTBArules20150601-110)

### United Kingdom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: United Kingdom")]

The [British Tenpin Bowling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Tenpin_Bowling_Association "British Tenpin Bowling Association") (BTBA, formed in 1961) is the official governing body recognized by [World Bowling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bowling "World Bowling") as the official sanctioning body in England, and as such "is responsible for the protection, integrity and development of the sport".[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BTBAabout-111) Its stated vision is "to ensure that all people, irrespective of their age, disability, ethnic origin, marital status, sexual orientation or social status have a genuine and equal opportunity to participate in the sport at all levels and in all roles".[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BTBAabout-111)

The [National Association of Youth Bowling Clubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Association_of_Youth_Bowling_Clubs?action=edit&redlink=1 "National Association of Youth Bowling Clubs (page does not exist)") (NAYBC) is a BTBA subcommittee serving youth bowlers and youth bowling clubs.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NAYBC-faq-112)

The British Universities Tenpin Bowling Association (BUTBA, formed in 2008) organizes bowling events for present and former university and college students.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-BUTBA-113)

The Tenpin Bowling Proprietors Association (TBPA, formed in 1961 as an [umbrella organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umbrella_organization "Umbrella organization")) is a [trade association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_association "Trade association") for the British ten-pin bowling industry.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-TBPAwhatis-114)

### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tenpin_bowling&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: United States")]

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Poster_of_the_first_bowling_competition%2C_1901.jpg/250px-Poster_of_the_first_bowling_competition%2C_1901.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Poster_of_the_first_bowling_competition,_1901.jpg)

Poster for the first national bowling competition sanctioned by the American Bowling Congress. Highest per-game average scores: individual competition (216), doubles (200), five-man teams (181).[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NYTimes_Scores_19010112-115) A protest was filed against the highest-scoring doubles team, alleging use of a ball that was a quarter-inch larger in circumference than permitted.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-NYTimes_Protest_19010112-116)

The [United States Bowling Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Bowling_Congress "United States Bowling Congress") (USBC) was formed as the governing body for the U.S. on January 1, 2005, by the merger of:[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenpin_bowling#cite_note-USBCmerger-117)

*   the American Bowling Congress (ABC, an originally male-only organization founded in 1895),

When I developed 3-point targeting with quiet eye, in 2006 & 2007, I knew it would help many bowlers enjoy the sport more and perform at a higher level. The original concept was published in several Bowling This Month articles in 2007 and early 2008. I brought the concept to the Kegel Training Center when I started working there in March of 2008. My Quiet Eye article was published just before I started at Kegel. 

To be effective, 3-point targeting with quiet eye must be paired with mathematically straight lines, which ensure the focal point and down-lane target are moved properly as you adjust to lane transition. With the teams and individuals I work with, I utilize my lane play alignment table to ensure the target and alignment movements correspond to what we intend to do as to see friction where we want to. 

Alignment, with mathematically straight lines, is also essential to ensure the ball encounters friction where you want it to. Moreover, this ensures straight lines paired with proper alignment that supports the development of the physical game not interferes with it negatively causing drift and swing issues over time when a bowler is constantly misaligned.

This process aids in pattern manipulation, starting on the fresh as well as dealing with lane transition.

Improving your bowling quickly requires focusing on repeatable fundamentals, small setup adjustments, and simple practice drills that transfer to games. The following actionable tips cover approach, release, ball selection, spare shooting, mental habits, and practice routines.

Stance and setup

*   Start with a relaxed, balanced stance: feet shoulder-width, knees slightly bent, ball held at waist or chest height. Avoid rigid shoulders or gripping the ball tightly.
*   Align your body to the spare target, not always to the head pin. For right-handers, play your initial alignment slightly left of your intended pocket (mirror for lefties) so your swing path can return to the pocket.
*   Use consistent marks on the approach (one or two anchor marks) so your starting step is repeatable.

Approach and timing

*   Use a 4-step or 5-step approach that matches your comfortable walking rhythm. Count steps aloud during practice until internalized.
*   Match the timing of your steps to your swing: step-swing-step-swing so your arm reaches the release at the moment your sliding foot stops.
*   Keep the approach smooth and relaxed. Rushed or jerky steps break timing and reduce accuracy.

Swing and release

*   Keep your arm swing pendulum-like: straight back and straight through, with minimal wrist deviation. This promotes consistency.
*   Let the ball swing; avoid forcing it forward with your shoulder. The power should come from the momentum of the swing and a relaxed push at release.
*   For hook shots: apply a firm but flexible wrist at release, rotating the fingers from 3 o’clock to 6 o’clock (for right-handers) while keeping the elbow close to the body.
*   For straight shots: keep fingers behind the ball, palm facing toward your target at release, and avoid rotation.
*   Aim for a clean, fingertip-driven release (using fingertip holes) if you want more lift and hook; conventional grip gives more control and less hook.

Footwork and finishing

*   Finish with a slide: the slide foot should stop and your body should be balanced, chest over the knee, and eyes on the target. A controlled follow-through improves accuracy.
*   Avoid standing up too early after release; keep low for sharper roll and better consistency.

Aiming and targeting

*   Use board and arrow aiming: arrows (15 feet from foul line) make consistent targeting easier than focusing on pins. Adjust based on ball reaction.
*   Move feet, not target: when adjusting line, shift your starting spot rather than changing your target to keep visual aiming consistent.
*   Track ball reaction: note where the ball first contacts the lane and where it reads the oil; adjust in small increments (one board or one-step changes).

Ball selection and equipment

*   Choose the right ball coverstock for lane conditions: polished/urethane for dry or burnt oil; reactive/resin with surface adjustments for medium to heavy oil.
*   Have at least two balls: a strong hooking ball and a control/backup ball for heavier conditions or carry shots.
*   Surface prep matters: use sanding/polish to tune reaction. Lower grit (e.g., 500–2000) for more friction/hook; higher grit (4000–4000+) for skid/flip.
*   Ensure proper fit and thumb/finger comfort—pain or slippage ruins release and consistency.

Spare shooting

*   Use a straight, controlled spare ball (plastic/urethane) for 2–8 pin conversions; keep the same target board for common spares.
*   Learn the “one-board left/right” rule: for many spares, moving the target one board equals a consistent path change. Create a simple chart for your most common spares.
*   Practice single-pin spares until you can hit them 9–10 out of 10; spares win matches.

Lane strategy and adjustments

*   Read the oil pattern early: if the ball hooks too much near the break point, move your feet toward the pocket or switch to a less aggressive ball; if it skids, move left (for right-handers) or use a higher-friction surface.
*   Make small, consistent adjustments—don’t overcorrect. One board or one step at a time.
*   Track carry, not style. If pin carry is good, don’t change a comfortable shot even if it “looks” awkward.

Mental game and routines

*   Have a pre-shot routine: same number of deep breaths, same stance, same visualization of the shot. Routines stabilize performance under pressure.
*   Focus on process (target, tempo, release) instead of outcomes (score). Let results be a byproduct.
*   Short-term memory: forget bad frames quickly. Reset with your routine and treat each shot independently.

Practice drills (high ROI)

*   Head-pin drill: throw 50 straight shots at the head pin using a plastic ball to build accuracy and spare confidence.
*   Spare-only game: bowl 10 frames using only spares; forces consistent spare mechanics and pressure practice.
*   Targeted repeatability: place a coin or sticker on an arrow or board and make 25 shots hitting that exact mark; reinforces consistent release and aim.
*   Breakpoint mapping: with your game ball, throw 10 shots and mark where the ball begins its hook; adjust starting position and repeat to learn how your ball reads oil.

Physical care and warm-up

*   Warm up with light stretching for shoulders, wrists, hips, and ankles. Bowl progressively—start with spare shots, then shorter swings, then full-power shots.
*   Manage grip pressure: maintain firm but not tense grip; tension reduces rotation and timing.
*   Maintain finger and wrist strength with resistance exercises and mobility work; prevents fatigue and preserves release consistency late in sessions.

Data and tracking

*   Record key metrics: strike percentage, spare conversion rate, first-ball strike carry, and how many boards you moved during the game. Small data points reveal patterns faster than intuition.
*   Video one session from behind and the side to self-diagnose timing, release, and approach inconsistencies.

Common quick fixes

*   Ball hooking too early: sand the surface a bit higher grit (make it smoother), or move right/left depending on handedness; try a plastic ball.
*   Ball sliding too long and flipping late: increase surface roughness or move toward the pocket; play more inside.
*   Leaves flat 10/7 pin: adjust axis rotation—less side roll—or move your target slightly toward the pocket to hit a firmer angle.

Examples (typical stories)

*   A league bowler raised spare conversion from 70% to 88% by dedicating two practice sessions weekly to spare-only drills and switching to a plastic spare ball.
*   A recreational player eliminated inconsistent hooks by adopting a 4-step approach, a consistent starting mark, and filming three sessions to identify early standing up in their follow-through.

Conclude with focus areas

*   Prioritize spare shooting and repeatable approach first; those yield the fastest scoring gains.
*   Use video and simple metrics to find small, fixable faults.
*   Make incremental changes—one adjustment at a time—and practice deliberately.

Knowledge note: strategy, equipment, and lane-reading principles reflect best practices current to May 2024.

I'm not sure whether this is frowned upon in the Quora Community, but here's an answer I gave to a similar question that may help you:

I'll do my best to give you some advice on how to get better (How to Progress in the Sport) and strategies (How to Read a Lane to Give you Better Striking Potential).

I am about to give you the two most powerful tips in bowling that everyone always seems to want to cast aside. People love talking about form, ball choice, generating revolutions on the ball, creating hook and everything under the sun. There are a million ways to get better at bowling. Look at the styles of Norm Duke, Chris Barnes, Sam Cooley and Osku Palermaa. The contrast is there, and it's obvious.

Practice Hitting Targets with a Consistent Setup

Bowling is nothing if not a formulaic game. As you get better, there are a million different methods of lane play that can impact ball motion and striking potential. That cornucopia of options that will test your skills, knowledge and creativity will never be open to you if you can't stand in a consistent spot, walk a consistent path and hit a consistent target. You don't have to walk straight. Look at Tom Smallwood or Michael Fagan. You don't have to have your shoulders super square at the line. Look at Sam Cooley and Jason Belmonte. You don't need to even look at a direct, one board target. Look at Sean Rash and Wes Malott. Rash draws lines and shapes on the lane to dictate ball motion, and Malott finds a breakpoint target, then follows his line all the way back to the foul line with his eyes. Brilliant bowlers take what they do naturally and turn it into striking power. Don't fight what's natural. Just be consistent with it.

Pay for a Good Coach

Most coaches suck. There's no way around it. Bowling has a huge problem: the number of people with good information versus the population of active players is abysmal. I didn't even have a set of moves until I got to college. I found better moves later, thanks to a helpful coach, but I had no idea that there was a distinct move I could make off of a four pin leave to get back to striking. Great coaches know a million moves, and they will know best what moves are right for you. Do not waste your time with non-USBC Certified Coaches. I do not care how high a person's average is, they will not have the strong, standardized knowledge base a USBC Certified Coach will have. You don't have to seek out a Gold Level Coach off the bat, but these coaches charge stupid amounts of money for a reason. They are truly great. Bad coaching ruined my game. Good coaching made me a competent collegiate bowler. Great coaching is getting me on my way to be the bowler I want to be later on. With enough practice and rapport, costs will shrink over time and lifelong bonds will translate into success.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Lane Play Basics

Lane Play can be a never ending quagmire of frustration and disappointment. Why is that guy striking like there's no tomorrow, and not me?! I'm throwing great shots, but nothing is going my way! This is a nightmare!

I've been there. One time, my ball reaction was so bad I shot 189 two games in a row. That's not the bad part. Those games were clean. That's not the worst part. I didn't strike once. I spent two straight games in a qualifying block shooting every single pin spare in the book. My carry in those games was terrible. Lane play is critical so that this doesn't happen to you.

Here is a set of pretty basic steps to read a lane:

1.   Play as Straight as you can

    1.   Pick the ball in the middle of your arsenal. Stand all the way right and throw the ball up the boards, and see what the ball does. A typical alignment for this would be standing with your feet at 9-12 and targeting 2-5. Playing this far out can be tricky. Practice it. After a couple shots, you will have two options: Changing Balls and Changing Alignment.
    2.   Changing Balls

    
        1.   You should know what shape your balls make when they are reactive well and striking. Weaker balls tend to be more angular. Strong balls tend to be smoother. If your ball is making the proper shape, but it's not hitting the pocket, change your alignment and not your ball. If your ball hooks so late down lane that it looks like it didn't see friction until it hit the pin deck, try a stronger ball. If the ball hooks at your feet, try a weaker ball. It's not rocket science. If your ball is making it through the front part of the lane well, but your ball is reacting like someone kicked it when it sees friction, a stronger ball might smooth that out. If the ball is getting to the right spot down lane, but looks lazy and slow when it makes its move, a weaker ball may help you get more hitting power into the pins.

    3.   Changing Alignment

    
        1.   If your ball is hooking in the right spot down the lane, but it isn't hitting the pins the way you want, we have to move your feet and target. The basic ideology is that if the ball goes left, you should do the same. If you throw a shot and the ball gets through the front part of the lane well, but you go Brooklyn, move your feet in a few boards and your target in a board or two. A good coach will be able to teach you moves off basic leaves and help you with your alignments, as no lane reacts the same.

In order to become a better bowler you have to have the following:

An approach. Whether it’s a four step approach or five or even six steps, you need to develop an approach to get to the foul line consistently. In order to determine where to stand place the heels of you shoes on the foul line and face opposite of the pins. Take natural steps, depending on how many steps you want to take in the approach, and then add a half step for the slide. I have a five step approach which works for my game. Power comes from your leg. Good drive and knee bend creates leverage to hook the ball.

Bowling ball. Choose a weight that is comfortable to you. If you want to take your game to the next level, then get your own all but for for house balls choose what is comfortable for you. Make sure to pick up the ball always with two hands in order to not tire out your bowling arm and using muscle in the approach.

Arm-swing. The idea is to have a straight arm swing that extends out towards your targets and you follow through to your target. Don’t look at the pins when you bowl. Identify a target, which is the arrows on the lane and try to hit that mark consistently.

Release. The thumb will come out naturally first. And then the fingers apply rotation on the ball. If you use a house ball, then simply staying behind the ball with a nice straight wrist will be sufficient.

Without getting into too much details, these are just a few tips when you bowl. Of course practice makes perfect. But only the right kind of practice which includes spare shooting, target practice and drills. Getting your own equipment even if it’s entry level equipment will make you become a better bowler!

Daniel Leonard [ https://www.quora.com/profile/Daniel-Leonard ] gave you a nice answer regarding equipement for balls and hands, I'll just add one thing in the same vein. Wipe your ball with a towel/microfiber towel to remove the oil on the surface. The ball should ideally be dry before every shot... for regularity.

In my opinion the best advices one can receive are regularity, precision and balance. This pretty much summarize how your playstyle should be. So do not try to walk fast to the foul line or throw the ball like a monkey. Your movement and swing should be smooth and natural. Not too quick, not too slow, try to keep it natural. I will consider you already played bowling for a few months if not more and have at least one strike ball and one spare ball.

As for your training, you usually need someone who can train you or at least help you, an outside view helps to see details and problems that you will not spot yourself. At some point filming yourself can also be a good idea, then by looking at it in slow motion you will see what is wrong or good with your approach, swing and follow through.

Always keep calm when playing, empty your head and focus, forget the people around you, the noises of the pins and or screams. My teacher used to stand on the lane or on the foul line to keep us focused.

There are a lot of exercices, usually two categories: those for spares and those for strikes. Strike exercices can include having to play on a specific oil pattern, aiming for a hook on a specific lane board, a hook past a mark, e.g a plastic cone. Also work on the rotation angles, rotation speed (you can measure it by filming and using a well placed bowling tape on your ball), follow through, etc...

For spares, there isn't much creativity, choose a spare system and practice every pocket, every pin and exotic spare too ...
